The photos showed clear signs of damage after the storm.
tattoo: a permanent design made on the skin with ink
He got a small tattoo of an anchor on his forearm.
looked: She looked through the old photographs for an hour.
like: similar to, or in the same way as
Her handwriting looks a lot like her mother's.
palm: a tropical tree with a tall trunk and large leaves at the top
A row of palm trees lined the sandy beach resort.
tree: a tall plant with a trunk, branches, and leaves
A mature tree shades the ground and releases water vapour at the same time.
said: past tense of say; spoke or expressed something in words
She said the meeting would start at nine o'clock.
ke: a Hindi grammatical particle roughly meaning 'of' or 'like'
từ nối tiếng Hindi (của, giống như)
The phrase used the word ke to link the two nouns together.
gachhi: a traditional tattoo design resembling a palm-tree pattern among Rana Tharu women
hình xăm cây cọ (theo truyền thống Tharu)
Her grandmother still wears a faded gachhi tattoo on her arm.
told: past tense of tell; communicated information to someone
A vessel sitting well above its red band is empty, and anyone can see that without being told.
me: used to refer to the speaker
Could you please pass me the salt?
past: gone by in time; belonging to an earlier time
Over the past year, the company has doubled its workforce.
cut: a line, opening, or channel made by cutting into something
Wildflowers soon appeared along the cut left by the new road.
down: toward a lower position or level
Please sit down and make yourself comfortable.
scrape: to rub something with a hard or sharp object to clean or remove it
Workers had to scrape years of paint off the old hull.
starchy: Potatoes and rice are both starchy foods.
core: the central or most essential part of something
Honesty remains at the core of every successful long-term relationship.
trunk: the main stem of a tree; the storage compartment of a car
They used to scrape the starchy core from the trunk of the palm tree.
prevalent: existing very commonly at a particular time or place
Smoking is far less prevalent among teenagers than it was decades ago.
southeastern: located in or relating to the southeast of an area
The southeastern part of the country receives the most rainfall.
countries: nations, each with its own government and territory
Trade agreements now link dozens of countries across three continents.
there: in, at, or to that place; used to show that something exists
There is a small cafe just around the corner.
heard: perceived sound with the ears; past tense of hear
She heard footsteps approaching from behind the door.
wider: measuring a larger distance from side to side
The gap between city and countryside grows wider still with added warmth.
audience: the group of people watching or listening to a performance
The audience clapped loudly at the end of the show.
recall: to remember something from the past
She could not recall where she had left her umbrella.
sitting: resting in a particular position or place for a period of time
The dishes were sitting in the sink for two whole days.
together: with each other; combined into one group or place
Sourdough relies on wild yeasts and bacteria living together in a starter.
fireside: the area around a fireplace, often associated with warmth and family
bên lò sưởi, cạnh bếp lửa
We spent winter evenings telling stories by the fireside.
chilly: unpleasantly cold; cool enough to cause discomfort
It was a chilly morning, so she wore an extra scarf.
